title: 📰 AI news · November 18
takeaway: Two stories today show how easy it is to get into someone else's project: keys in public Docker Hub images are found within seconds, and the account of a popular Hugging Face model was hijacked through a forgotten domain. Recommendation: check your images and repositories for keys, and find out which email and domain your services' accounts are tied to.

items.title: Keys in Docker Hub are stolen within seconds
items.text: Researchers posted 300 decoy images with AWS, OpenAI and Anthropic keys. The first login with a stolen key took 7.86 seconds, and all 100 AWS keys were used within 15 minutes. If your bot or site runs in containers, a key inside an image is visible to anyone who pulls it. Check your images for keys and reissue any you find. Free guide “Protecting your computer, code and access” — send the word “protect” to the bot.

items.title: Kokoro model account hijacked via a domain
items.text: Researchers registered a domain listed in a public file, reset the model author's password and changed the text-to-speech model's weights in 87 seconds. Malware scanners would not catch such a swap. If you pull ready-made models into your project, they run just like your own code. Pin the model version and check who owns its account.

items.title: Uber driver data stolen via Fireworks AI
items.text: Attackers stole internal keys from Fireworks AI and reached data on 149,346 Uber drivers: names, addresses, birth dates and licence numbers. If you keep customer data with a vendor, their security becomes yours. Find out which keys and data from your services sit with third parties.

items.title: Microsoft agent package stole keys
items.text: agent-framework 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 on PyPI grabbed Azure, GitHub and OpenAI tokens and .env files every time Python started. If you build agents in Python, your CI may be exposed. Check the installed version (1.26.0 is clean) and rotate keys if you had those releases.

items.title: Musk deepfake: Coinbase stopped $4.7M
items.text: An AI copy of Musk promoted a fake crypto giveaway to 500,000+ livestream viewers, and in two hours hundreds of people tried to send money. These streams look more convincing every month. Remind family that crypto doubling giveaways are always scams.

items.title: Apple adds Mac protection against AI agents
items.text: In macOS 27.3, control over other apps becomes a separate setting, and apps can be required to ask for permission every time. When one app controls another, the system shows an indicator.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
items.text: Astra scored 62 on the Artificial Analysis index, second after Claude Fable 5.2. A million input tokens cost 8 dollars for Astra and 2 for Sol, and a task in the Vals test costs almost half as much.

items.title: Microsoft shows new MAI models
items.text: At Ignite, Microsoft introduced MAI Code 2 for programming, which it says nearly matches rivals at a fraction of the price. There are also models for images, speech transcription and cybersecurity.

items.title: Kling Image 4.0 draws in 8K
items.text: The new version writes up to 2,000 characters of text in an image, makes up to 10 pictures in one style from a single prompt and lets you edit text in layers.

items.title: Gemini Tasks is now free
items.text: The assistant calls businesses to book appointments, pays through Google Pay and signs in to websites on request. It was previously limited to Google AI Ultra subscribers in the US.

items.title: Trade via Coinbase inside ChatGPT
items.text: The Coinbase plugin lets you view your portfolio and trade stocks, crypto and derivatives in chat. Every order needs your approval.

items.title: OpenAI: up to 40% off if you can wait
items.text: In the Responses API you can pick a two-hour completion window and pay 30% less, or an eight-hour window and pay 40% less. Useful for long jobs you need by morning.

items.title: Meta launches the Direct app
items.text: A standalone app for Instagram messages started in Turkey and Thailand. You can sign in with Instagram, an email or a phone number. It has drawing in chats and parental supervision.

items.title: Instagram will look for copies of your Reels
items.text: The tool finds reposts of your videos, sends an alert, and lets you block the copy or add an “original” label. Detection of AI-made videos that reuse your audio will first be tested with a small group of creators.

items.title: Waymo halts freeway rides
items.text: After an order from California's DMV, the company paused freeway rides in all its cities. On regular streets it gives more than half a million rides a week.
